objective: Test whether adding one cross-asset defensive-trend sleeve (D1 Carlson Defense First TAA rotation, D2 12-month-vs-SHY absolute momentum with inverse-63-session-vol sizing) to the live S3 leveraged-momentum sleeve, combined by trailing-63-session inverse-volatility monthly weighting, beats delevering S3 alone to the same realized volatility (K2, owner-widened >=0.05 bar) in both the anchor and stress windows, or, failing that, whether either sleeve is standalone-competitive with S3 (K1).

sources.core_claim: Carlson (2025) 'Defense First: A Multi-Asset Tactical Model for Adaptive Downside Protection' is a 2025 SSRN preprint; primary text not retrievable, rules pinned from independent replications.
sources.project_applicability: Confirms D1's mechanism is a real, dated, citable published model rather than an unattributed rule.
sources.reflection: Reused unchanged from H-20260923-12 (dir:defense_first_taa_carlson_concretum); snapshot copied into this dossier's sources/, not re-fetched.

sources.core_claim: Defense First: rank TLT/GLD/DBC(or PDBC)/UUP by the average of 1/3/6/12-month returns at month-end close; weight 40/30/20/10 by rank; any asset below T-bill (BIL) momentum has its tier weight redirected to SPY; rebalance monthly regardless of change.
sources.project_applicability: Pins D1's exact momentum definition, rank-weight table, hurdle/fallback rule and rebalance cadence, reused unedited from run_h20260923_12_s3_defense_first.py's defense_weights().
sources.reflection: Reused unchanged from H-20260923-12; independent replication of the SSRN preprint.

sources.core_claim: The author's own announcement confirms the four-ETF menu (TLT, GLD, DBC, UUP) with SPY fallback, using DBC (not AllocateSmartly's PDBC substitute).
sources.project_applicability: Deciding source for D1's use of DBC, which is present in the local SIP daily archive.

sources.core_claim: A second independent replication of Defense First reports materially higher CAGR than SPY at matched volatility (3x-leveraged-fallback variant: 16.2% vs 10.6%) with a better Sharpe and much smaller drawdowns.
sources.project_applicability: Triangulates that the mechanism is real (three independent replications: Quantitativo, AllocateSmartly, and BestFolio per the registry), not a single blogger's artifact.
sources.reflection: Reused unchanged from H-20260923-12; not used for D1's exact rule text (AllocateSmartly is used for that).

sources.core_claim: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen (2012) document time-series momentum: an asset's own trailing 12-month excess return positively predicts its own future return across 58 diverse futures/forward contracts over 25+ years, positive for every single instrument examined.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds D2's own-asset absolute-momentum mechanism (hold when trailing 12-month return beats the SHY cash proxy) as a peer-reviewed, independently documented anomaly, not a home-grown rule.
sources.reflection: Freshly fetched this pass (curl snapshot); quote binding recorded in direction-review.json and the source_cards jsonl.

sources.core_claim: Hurst, Ooi and Pedersen (2017) extend trend-following evidence back to 1880, finding the strategy consistently profitable across the following ~110 years and performing well in 8 of the 10 largest historical crisis periods, with low correlation to traditional benchmarks -- while flagging rising cross-market correlation since the credit crisis as a headwind.
sources.project_applicability: Motivates evaluating D1/D2 across the full stress period (2018Q4, 2020, 2022 drawdowns included) and reporting 2022-specific correlation with S3, and grounds the caution that trend-following's edge can compress as correlations rise -- exactly what the K2 diversifier test checks for locally.
sources.reflection: Freshly fetched this pass (curl snapshot); quote binding recorded in direction-review.json and the source_cards jsonl.

sources.core_claim: Inverse-volatility weighting -- weighting return streams by the reciprocal of their trailing realized volatility -- is a standard, simple way to combine multiple return streams when their expected Sharpe ratios and pairwise correlations are similar.
sources.project_applicability: Direct precedent for D2's inverse-63-session-volatility sizing rule and for the S3+D combination weight (screen_lane.combine_two_sleeves, ported unedited from H-20260927-01's combine_portfolio).
sources.reflection: Already catalogued and used identically in H-20260927-01's external-brief.json; not re-fetched this pass, cited for descriptive precedent only.

sources.core_claim: A levered/diversified portfolio scaled to match a concentrated alternative's own volatility level can outperform that alternative, illustrating that diversification's value must be judged against a volatility-matched comparison, not against the concentrated portfolio at its own natural risk.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds this round's reused K2 combination methodology (screen_lane's vol-matched k*S3+(1-k)*SHY control, ported from H-20260927-01), which this round applies unchanged to D1/D2.
sources.reflection: Already catalogued and verified in H-20260927-01's source cards; not re-fetched this pass, cited for the comparison-methodology precedent this round reuses.

candidate_matrix_revisions.effect: D1 uses Carlson's published rank weights (40/30/20/10), momentum blend (1/3/6/12-month), BIL hurdle and SPY fallback unchanged -- reused directly from run_h20260923_12_s3_defense_first.defense_weights, generalized to evaluate at any signal date so the batch harness's 21 rebalance-day offsets can each be swept without look-ahead.

D2's rule (hold TLT/GLD/DBC/UUP only when its own trailing 12-month return beats SHY's) is set as the queue task's stated round numbers, not tuned to this paper's own parameters -- the paper only grounds the mechanism (own-asset absolute momentum) as peer-reviewed, not the specific 12-month/63-session thresholds.
